purpose: Selected source-backed constraints for blocking out a model. The full catalogue is broader; no coordinates or complete floor plan are asserted here.

constraints.subject: Castle
constraints.object: High mountain/cliff above the lake
constraints.description: The first lake view places the many-turreted, many-towered castle high above the water, on a mountain and then explicitly on a cliff.
constraints.model_notes: Preserve substantial elevation and a cliff-facing lake approach. The text supplies neither contour elevations nor a complete shoreline or compass bearing.

constraints.subject: First-year boat route
constraints.object: Ivy-hidden cliff opening and dark tunnel to underground harbour
constraints.description: The boats enter a broad cliff opening behind ivy, travel along a dark tunnel seemingly beneath the castle, and land at an underground harbour with rocks and pebbles.
constraints.model_notes: The impression that the tunnel goes under the castle is qualified in the narration. Do not replace the harbour with an exposed film boathouse.

constraints.subject: Underground harbour
constraints.object: Rising rock passage, grass, stone steps, oak front door
constraints.description: From the landing, students climb a rock passage to damp grass in the castle's shadow, then ascend stone steps to the large oak front door.
constraints.model_notes: Keep this traversable sequence. Passage length, exact exit position, and overlap with the carriage approach remain design variables.

constraints.subject: Main gates
constraints.object: Long rising drive to castle entrance
constraints.description: Wrought-iron gates are flanked by stone columns carrying winged boars. Carriages ascend a long sloping drive; the oak front doors stand above stone steps.
constraints.model_notes: Gate design and a rising approach are constrained. Do not infer a measured distance or a straight drive from the arrival alone.

constraints.subject: Main gates
constraints.object: Road into Hogsmeade
constraints.description: Walking out between the boar-topped pillars, students turn left onto the road into the village.
constraints.model_notes: Left is relative to the direction of exit; it is not a compass bearing.

constraints.subject: Hagrid's cabin
constraints.object: Forbidden Forest edge below sloping lawns
constraints.description: Students descend the sloping lawns to Hagrid's hut at the edge of the Forbidden Forest; another visit describes the cabin as small and wooden.
constraints.model_notes: Preserve the downhill castle-to-cabin route and forest adjacency without choosing a compass quadrant from adaptation imagery.

constraints.subject: Herbology greenhouses
constraints.object: Castle
constraints.description: Herbology takes place in greenhouses behind the castle. A later flight across the grounds passes vegetable gardens, greenhouses, the Whomping Willow, then forest shelter.
constraints.model_notes: Behind is a viewpoint-relative description. The travel sequence gives connectivity and proximity rather than a surveyed straight line.

constraints.subject: Lakeside beech
constraints.object: Window beside Neville's bed
constraints.description: A large beech shades a study spot at the lake edge. Harry later sees the same tree directly ahead from the window beside Neville's bed.
constraints.temporal: Book 5; tree also identified in a school memory
constraints.model_notes: Use a line-of-sight constraint between a particular Gryffindor dormitory window and this tree. It does not locate every tower window or the whole shoreline.

constraints.subject: Dumbledore's tomb
constraints.object: Lake
constraints.description: At the funeral, white flames leave a white marble tomb around the body and its table. A later visit places it beside the lake, reflected in the water.
constraints.temporal: Added at end of Book 6; present in Book 7
constraints.model_notes: This is a dated addition. Earlier school-year scenes should omit it. No source-backed footprint dimensions are supplied by these passages.

constraints.subject: Entrance Hall
constraints.object: Flagged stone floor, torchlit stone walls, very high ceiling, marble staircase
constraints.description: The Entrance Hall is extremely large, with a ceiling too high for Harry to make out. A marble staircase faces the arriving group and leads to upper floors.
constraints.model_notes: The comparison to the Dursleys' house communicates scale without providing a reliable measurement. Preserve material, volume, and approach-facing staircase.

constraints.subject: Entrance Hall arrival
constraints.object: Doorway carrying the Great Hall's crowd noise
constraints.description: Crossing the Entrance Hall on arrival, Harry hears the school through a doorway to the right. McGonagall first leads the newcomers into a small empty chamber off the hall.
constraints.model_notes: Keep the small waiting chamber separate from the Great Hall and from later rooms behind the staff table. Right is relative to this approach.

constraints.subject: Great Hall
constraints.object: Four long house tables and a staff table at the top
constraints.description: Thousands of floating candles illuminate four student tables set with gold plates and goblets. A further long table seats the teachers at the top of the Hall. The ceiling looks like the starry sky; Hermione explains the enchantment.
constraints.model_notes: The ceiling's appearance is observed; its explanation is reported dialogue within the same passage. Do not assign an unsupported hall length or permanent table orientation beyond the staff-table relationship.

constraints.subject: Kitchens
constraints.object: Great Hall
constraints.description: The kitchens form an enormous high-ceilinged room as large as the Great Hall above, with stone walls, brass cookware and a large brick fireplace at the far end. Four wooden tables correspond exactly to the four house tables overhead.
constraints.model_notes: Stack the two spaces and align the four table positions. Food transmission through the ceiling is Harry's supposition here; a visible shaft or lift is not established.

constraints.subject: Kitchen approach
constraints.object: Entrance Hall to bright food-painted stone corridor
constraints.description: Descending the marble staircase into the Entrance Hall, Hermione turns left at its bottom, uses a doorway, and descends stone steps to a broad torchlit corridor painted with food pictures. Tickling the green pear in the fruit-bowl painting produces a green door handle.
constraints.model_notes: Maintain this local sequence and interaction. The route is explicitly contrasted with the gloomy passage to Snape's dungeon, so do not merge the two solely because both descend.

constraints.subject: Gryffindor entrance
constraints.object: Seventh floor at the Fat Lady's portrait
constraints.description: The flight from the forbidden third-floor room ends at the Fat Lady's portrait on the seventh floor.
constraints.model_notes: This fixes an entrance level, not the count of complete floors throughout every tower. Use British floor numbering consistently.

constraints.subject: Gryffindor boys' dormitory
constraints.object: Spiral staircase from common room
constraints.description: Separate doors lead girls and boys towards their dormitories. Harry's tower dormitory is above a spiral staircase and contains five four-posters with deep-red velvet hangings; later narration identifies a circular room with high, narrow windows.
constraints.model_notes: Five beds describe this particular cohort's room. Do not extrapolate identical capacities or all other rooms' geometry without their own evidence.

constraints.subject: Slytherin common room
constraints.object: Sliding stone door concealed in damp bare wall
constraints.description: A spoken password opens a concealed stone door. Beyond lies a long, low underground room with rough stone walls and ceiling, greenish round lamps on chains, a fire below an ornate carved mantelpiece, and carved chairs.
constraints.model_notes: These passages establish an underground room. They do not establish large underwater viewing windows; any such addition needs other textual evidence.

constraints.subject: Hufflepuff route
constraints.object: Basement corridor also leading to kitchens
constraints.description: On the Marauder's Map, Harry follows the Hufflepuffs back to the basement corridor also used to reach the kitchens. The Ravenclaws return to a west-side tower, and Gryffindors to the Fat Lady along the corridor.
constraints.model_notes: This is useful comparative route evidence. It does not describe a Hufflepuff common-room interior or its door mechanism.

constraints.subject: Ravenclaw common room
constraints.object: Tight spiral stair and eagle-knocker door
constraints.description: The climb winds tightly to an old wooden door with no handle or keyhole and a bronze eagle knocker. Entry is granted after a reasoned answer to a question.
constraints.model_notes: The earlier fifth-floor exit from the Room of Requirement is not itself the common-room floor. Preserve the intervening route and ascent.

constraints.subject: Ravenclaw common room
constraints.object: Arched windows, blue/bronze silks, star dome and carpet, white marble founder statue
constraints.description: The room is wide, circular and airy, with graceful arched windows, blue and bronze wall silks, a domed star-painted ceiling and matching midnight-blue carpet, tables, chairs and bookcases. Rowena's white marble statue stands opposite the entrance by another door.
constraints.model_notes: The mountain view by day is a narrative projection from this night-time visit. Harry only guesses that the adjacent door leads to dormitories above; retain that qualification.

constraints.subject: Divination classroom
constraints.object: Top of North Tower above trapdoor and ladder
constraints.description: The North Tower approach ends at a tiny landing without doors. A circular ceiling trapdoor labelled for Trelawney admits a descending silver ladder. Above is a circular, heavily furnished room with at least twenty small round tables, armchairs and pouffes, red-shaded light, closed curtains and a scented fire.
constraints.model_notes: The name/location comes from the timetable dialogue and journey; room fixtures are directly observed. The seven staircases climbed on this unfamiliar route do not prove exactly seven storeys.

constraints.subject: North Tower approach landing
constraints.object: A visible part of the lake
constraints.description: At the unfamiliar landing, Ron rejects a passage because it heads south and points to a bit of lake visible through the window.
constraints.model_notes: Treat as a useful local orientation report, with Ron's navigation uncertainty. It does not establish a complete north-up site plan.

constraints.subject: Owlery
constraints.object: Top of West Tower
constraints.description: The Owlery is at the top of West Tower: a circular stone room with glassless windows, cold draughts, straw/droppings/bones underfoot, and owl perches rising towards the tower top.
constraints.model_notes: Represent the draughty open windows and vertical perches. No exact tower diameter or independently surveyed position is supplied here.

constraints.subject: Flitwick's office
constraints.object: Seventh floor, thirteenth window relative to West Tower
constraints.description: Dumbledore directs the rescuers to Flitwick's seventh-floor office with a window-count instruction involving West Tower. Harry later counts windows to the right of that tower.
constraints.model_notes: Preserve both the instruction's wording and the observed counting action in source inspection; do not turn an ambiguous right/from-right reference into an unquestioned façade coordinate.

constraints.subject: Astronomy Tower
constraints.object: Castle towers
constraints.description: The Astronomy Tower is named as the castle's highest tower. Its top has crenellated ramparts and a door with an iron ring giving access to a spiral staircase back into the castle.
constraints.model_notes: Maintain a relative height ordering and a usable stair door. The rooftop scene does not provide the tower's absolute height or all surrounding roof levels.

constraints.subject: Castle circulation
constraints.object: 142 varied staircases and conditional doors/routes
constraints.description: The castle has 142 staircases of varied forms. Some lead to different destinations on Fridays or contain a vanishing step; doors may respond to polite requests or tickling, while apparent doors may be solid walls. Portrait subjects visit other frames.
constraints.model_notes: The stated count is firm; the distribution is not. Support conditional connections and steps. This passage does not require the film's large rotating staircase mechanism. The armour's mobility is Harry's belief here, not equally firm observation.

constraints.subject: Room of Requirement entrance
constraints.object: Barnabas tapestry on seventh floor
constraints.description: The meeting place is on the seventh floor opposite the tapestry of Barnabas and the trolls. Three concentrated passes along a blank wall, between a window and a large vase, produce a polished door with a brass handle.
constraints.model_notes: Keep a stable external anchor and implement the interior as a requested state rather than assigning all incarnations one fixed ordinary room.

constraints.subject: DA practice room
constraints.object: Spacious torchlit room with bookcases, cushions and detectors
constraints.description: In its practice state the Room of Requirement is spacious and torchlit, with wall bookcases, silk floor cushions and dark detectors on shelves at the far end. The torches are compared to those in dungeons eight floors below.
constraints.model_notes: The eight-floor comparison supplies a relative level clue. Do not use it to solve every basement or wing into one uniform section.

constraints.subject: Room of Requirement refuge
constraints.object: DA hideout and Hog's Head passage
constraints.description: The refuge has wood-panelled windowless walls, a balcony, multicoloured hammocks, house hangings, books and a wireless. Neville explains its growth with new arrivals and the appearance of a food-supply passage to Aberforth; Seamus reports added hammocks and a bathroom.
constraints.model_notes: The observed interior is explicit; growth, entry protections and passage creation are residents' reports. The room does not simply conjure food in this account.

constraints.subject: Hog's Head passage
constraints.object: Ariana portrait above fireplace to Room of Requirement
constraints.description: The route begins behind Ariana's portrait above the mantelpiece, passes smooth stone steps into a brass-lamped passage with a worn earth floor, later climbs steeply, and ends with another short stair and concealed door into the refuge.
constraints.model_notes: Treat as a later-created connection, separate from the earlier seven passages. Distance and how it fits physically into exterior terrain remain unconstrained.

constraints.subject: Room of Requirement exit used by Harry and Luna
constraints.object: Fifth-floor corridor
constraints.description: A long torchlit stair with unexpected turns leads from the refuge to a wall which melts open and reseals. The Marauder's Map places Harry and Luna in a fifth-floor corridor.
constraints.model_notes: Do not relocate the regular seventh-floor entrance to reconcile this. Model a state-dependent exit and its connecting stair.

constraints.subject: Earlier secret passages
constraints.object: Seven, with blocked and guarded variants
constraints.description: Fred describes seven passages, four known to Filch, one behind a fourth-floor mirror blocked since the preceding winter, one under the Whomping Willow, and one from the one-eyed witch to Honeydukes' cellar. Neville later reports the older passages sealed and guarded.
constraints.model_notes: Do not invent destinations for the four unnamed routes or reuse one fixed open/closed state across all years.

constraints.subject: Honeydukes passage entrance
constraints.object: Third-floor corridor in one-eyed humpbacked witch statue
constraints.description: The statue is halfway along the third-floor corridor. The map demonstrates tapping it with a wand and speaking Dissendium to open access.
constraints.model_notes: This supplies an entrance anchor and interaction. It does not specify the entire tunnel's plan or measured length.

constraints.subject: Whomping Willow tunnel
constraints.object: Shrieking Shack
constraints.description: Lupin explains that the house and tunnel were prepared for his transformations and the tree placed at the tunnel mouth to keep people out. Prodding a knot on the trunk makes entry possible.
constraints.temporal: Book 3 explanation of earlier school history
constraints.model_notes: The route must coexist with dated tree activity and an operable knot interaction. Keep historical explanation distinct from a surveyed route.

constraints.subject: Hogwarts Apparition protection
constraints.object: Apparition and Disapparition inside grounds
constraints.description: Hermione states that one cannot Apparate within the Hogwarts grounds. During lessons, the instructor explains a one-hour exception confined to the Great Hall. Fleeing attackers later head for gates beyond which they can Disapparate.
constraints.model_notes: Use boundary- and state-dependent travel rules. The flight towards the gates is narrated action, while the enchantment's rule is explained in dialogue.

constraints.subject: Castle seen by Muggles
constraints.object: Decaying ruin with danger sign
constraints.description: Hermione explains that a Muggle looking at Hogwarts sees an old ruin with an unsafe-entry warning.
constraints.model_notes: An optional Muggle-view rendering can use this. The following speculation about making a school Unplottable concerns Durmstrang; do not silently transfer that claim to Hogwarts.

constraints.subject: Quidditch goals
constraints.object: Fifty feet
constraints.description: The school stadium has raised seating around the pitch and three golden hooped poles at each end, described as fifty feet high.
constraints.model_notes: This is a useful absolute scale anchor: 50 feet equals 15.24 metres. It does not establish the pitch's length, width, or stand heights.

constraints.subject: Beauxbatons carriage
constraints.object: Hagrid's front door: two hundred yards
constraints.description: The large powder-blue carriage is parked two hundred yards from Hagrid's front door, with a makeshift paddock for its winged horses alongside it.
constraints.model_notes: Use as a temporary placement constraint (200 yards equals 182.88 metres), not a permanent building or precise surveyed bearing.

constraints.subject: Fifth-floor east-wing corridor
constraints.object: Weasley swamp and ferry route
constraints.description: The twins' swamp fills a fifth-floor corridor in the east wing. The area is roped off and Filch must ferry students across to their classrooms.
constraints.model_notes: Keep the corridor's ordinary traversal separate from the temporary water crossing. The passage gives a wing and floor, not an overall east-wing footprint.

constraints.subject: Myrtle's toilet
constraints.object: First floor in Book 2; second floor in Book 4
constraints.description: Hermione places Myrtle's girls' toilet on the first floor in Book 2. Book 4 narration describes her as haunting the girls' toilets on the second floor.
constraints.model_notes: The conflict is explicit in the two sources, though the Book 2 location is dialogue. Keep both constraints and label any chosen implementation. Do not claim that a moving room or floor-renumbering explanation is itself stated canon.
